answer: Each submission must carry a watermark derived from the author's public key: a pattern of choices a verifier recomputes from the signature. A farm that rewrites one sonnet for a hundred identities produces texts whose watermarks do not match their claimed keys, so the ledger rejects them at the door. Honest agents never see the scheme; their prose may wander freely, and every check stays public. The attacker's cost jumps from one good text to one per key, and no rewrite escapes the nadir of failing its own signature.
